1-1-1: Good meals today; the story around them is ready to grow

You serve balanced meals and encourage healthy eating and less waste. Little yet involves students, families or the wider community: nutrition education, sustainability and communication are all informal.
Start with communication: share menus and a monthly food update, and run a short feedback survey each term. Then add one hands-on activity, such as a cooking session.
Visible activity around food gives you stories to share at every parent meeting.
What families hear about your cafeteria shapes how they talk about the institution as a whole.
Parents feel informed and heard, and students start to take part rather than just eat.
1-1-3: Communication is under way; education and sustainability come next
Regular updates and feedback surveys show that you value what families think. Nutrition education and sustainability, though, are still limited to reminders.
Add a termly hands-on nutrition activity and one measurable green initiative, such as tracking plate waste, and report both in your updates.
Your updates gain real news to share.
Updates that show real progress turn your communication into reputation.
Families see more than menus: they see a programme taking shape.

Strong communication multiplies the value of every initiative you add.
Families stay engaged when there is always something new to see.
